title: OAuth revoke must verify token belongs to requesting client before any revoke path
answers: Can one OAuth client revoke another app's token at /oauth/revoke/?
Why does revoking a token from a different client_id return 200 but do nothing?
Where is RFC 7009 client binding enforced for token revocation?
body:
Invariant: `revoke_token` in posthog/api/oauth/views.py must first look up the presented token (refresh, else access) and, if its `application_id` != `request.client.pk`, log `oauth_revoke_token_client_mismatch` and return without revoking.
- The check must run before the DCR/CIMD session sweep (`revoke_oauth_session`) and before `super().revoke_token(...)`. django-oauth-toolkit upstream revokes any token found by value, so skipping the check lets any client end another app's session.
- Mismatch must still yield HTTP 200 (same as an unknown token). An error response would reveal that the token is live for another client.
- Applies to both token types and all client types (public, confidential, DCR, CIMD).
- Limitation: public clients authenticate with client_id only, so a holder of the token who knows the owner's public client_id can still revoke.
applies: posthog/api/oauth/views.py revoke_token and any new revoke/introspect-style OAuth endpoint logic

search: The `revoke_token()` function in posthog/api/oauth/views.py must verify the presented token (refresh or access) belongs to the requesting client by checking that `token.application_id == request.client.pk` before any revoke operation; if the check fails, log `oauth_revoke_token_client_mismatch` and return HTTP 200 without revoking. This check must run before the DCR/CIMD session sweep (`revoke_oauth_session`) and before calling `super().revoke_token()`, because the upstream django-oauth-toolkit revokes any token found by value, allowing a malicious client to revoke another application's session. Mismatch must return HTTP 200 (not an error) to avoid leaking information about token liveness to other clients. Public clients using only client_id authentication remain vulnerable to revocation if a token holder knows the owner's public client_id. Applies to posthog/api/oauth/views.py and any new revoke/introspect-style OAuth endpoints.
